title: #stitch with @ash sees all the theater This has been haunting me! #di...
transcript: I've been racking my brain trying to come up with some semblance of a logical explanation for why some people might think that animated musicals don't count as musicals, and the best that I can come up with is that I think there are a lot of people who the especially musical theater, is not a big part of their life who the quality they most strongly associate with the experience of watching a musical is the suspension of disbelief, the fantasy of people breaking out into song. And animated musicals maybe don't have that because they're already so far removed from reality that the singing is like the least fantastical thing about it. Whether you enjoy musicals or not, if that's the feeling that you most strongly associate with them, I can sort of see how they're separate in your mind. I guess. There is a long history of cartoons just including songs a little more casually and loosely without adhering to those story conventions. So I can see how if you're not paying attention to those nuances, a full animated musical can maybe just feel like an extension of that. I don't know.
classificationReason: A meta-discussion about whether animated musicals 'count' as musicals, prompted by a stitch with another creator. No specific stage production is reviewed or discussed; purely a genre/conceptual debate.
